description: Adapt the recipe-photo edge function to use Unsplash as the primary image provider, keeping Pexels as a fallback and preserving graceful degradation. Add the Unsplash-required download trigger (best-effort) and expose attribution fields in the response, without breaking the existing Flutter client that only reads data['url']. No new migration and no Flutter client changes required for the minimal viable path.
steps: Edit supabase/functions/recipe-photo/index.ts. Keep the entire existing security pattern intact: Deno.serve, CORS headers, OPTIONS handling, POST-only, read SUPABASE_URL/SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, validate JWT via admin.auth.getUser(jwt), require profile + home_id, read {query}. Do NOT consume AI credit. Preserve the top-level try/catch that degrades to {url:null} on any unexpected error.

Provider selection after validating the query: read const unsplashKey = Deno.env.get('UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY') and const pexelsKey = Deno.env.get('PEXELS_API_KEY'). If unsplashKey is set, use Unsplash. Else if pexelsKey is set, use the existing Pexels path (keep it as-is). Else return json({ url: null }) with status 200. Never return 500 for a missing key or provider failure.

Implement the Unsplash path in its own helper (e.g. async function searchUnsplash(query, key)). Call GET `https://api.unsplash.com/search/photos?query=${encodeURIComponent(query)}&per_page=1&orientation=landscape` with header { Authorization: `Client-ID ${key}` }. Wrap the whole thing in try/catch; on fetch exception, non-ok res, or no results, return { url: null } (console.error the status/body for diagnostics, matching the existing Pexels logging style).

Parse the Unsplash response: const results = Array.isArray(data?.results) ? data.results : []; if empty -> { url: null }. Take first = results[0]. photoUrl = first?.urls?.regular ?? first?.urls?.small ?? null. Also read attribution: photographerName = first?.user?.name ?? null; photographerUrl = first?.user?.links?.html ?? null; unsplashUrl = 'https://unsplash.com'. Read downloadLocation = first?.links?.download_location (string | undefined).

Unsplash DOWNLOAD TRIGGER (required by Unsplash API guidelines when a photo is 'used'/selected): if downloadLocation is a non-empty string, fire GET downloadLocation with header { Authorization: `Client-ID ${key}` } as BEST-EFFORT. It must NOT block or break the response: do not await it in a way that can throw into the main path, or if awaited, wrap in its own try/catch that swallows errors (console.error only). A failure of the trigger must still return the photo url normally. Add a clear comment explaining WHY (Unsplash terms require triggering the download endpoint on photo usage).

Response shape: return json({ url: photoUrl, provider: 'unsplash', attribution: { photographer: photographerName, photographerUrl, source: 'Unsplash', sourceUrl: unsplashUrl } }). When photoUrl is null, return json({ url: null }) (attribution omitted or null is fine). Rationale: the existing Flutter client reads ONLY data['url'] (lib/add_recipe_screen.dart ~line 480, lib/discover_recipes_screen.dart ~line 130), so adding extra fields is backward-compatible and requires no client change. Document in a comment that persisting/displaying full attribution (photographer credit UI) is a documented future enhancement; the technically-required download trigger is implemented now.

Update the file's top banner comment: explain the Unsplash-first / Pexels-fallback / degrade-to-null behavior, the Client-ID auth format, the download-trigger requirement, that the UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY secret is set from the Supabase web panel, and remove/replace the old 'supabase functions deploy recipe-photo (lo hace la usuaria)' instruction since deploy is now automated by CI (keep wording consistent with the docs updated in FEAT-003).
Do NOT modify lib/ files unless strictly necessary. The minimal viable path keeps saving only the URL into image_url (externalImageUrl). Do NOT add a new migration.

Reason through and (in findings) document the behavior for each case: (a) no key at all -> {url:null} 200; (b) UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY present, happy path -> {url, attribution} and download trigger fired; (c) only PEXELS_API_KEY present -> existing Pexels behavior unchanged; (d) Unsplash network/5xx/4xx failure -> {url:null} 200; (e) Unsplash returns zero results -> {url:null} 200; (f) download trigger throws/fails -> photo url still returned normally.
acceptance_criteria: recipe-photo/index.ts uses Unsplash when UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY is set (endpoint search/photos, per_page=1, orientation=landscape, Authorization: Client-ID <key>).
When only PEXELS_API_KEY is set, the previous Pexels behavior is preserved.
When neither key is set, the function returns { url: null } with status 200.
Any Unsplash fetch failure, non-ok response, or empty results degrades to { url: null } status 200 (never 500).
The Unsplash download_location endpoint is triggered best-effort with the Client-ID header, and a failure there does not affect the returned url.
Response includes the photo url under data.url (so the existing Flutter client keeps working unchanged) plus attribution fields (photographer name + profile link + Unsplash source link).
JWT validation, home_id requirement, CORS, and no-AI-credit behavior are unchanged; no new migration is added.
flutter analyze stays at 0 issues, dart format reports no changes, and flutter test stays green (Dart side untouched).
verification: Confirm TypeScript reads Deno.env.get('UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY') and uses the Client-ID auth header and search/photos endpoint.
Confirm the download trigger is wrapped so its failure cannot break the response.
Confirm the Pexels fallback branch is still present and unchanged in behavior.
findings: Implementado en supabase/functions/recipe-photo/index.ts (commit 27527b9 sobre feat/recetas-rediseno). Unsplash es el proveedor principal via helper searchUnsplash(query,key); Pexels queda como respaldo con su codigo intacto. No se tocaron archivos lib/, no se anadio migracion. No hay runner de Deno/TS ni Deno instalado, asi que la verificacion de la edge function es por razonamiento. Casos razonados: (a) sin ninguna clave -> Deno.serve devuelve json({url:null}) status 200 en la rama 4b (!pexelsKey). (b) UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY presente y camino feliz -> searchUnsplash hace GET search/photos?query=...&per_page=1&orientation=landscape con header Authorization: Client-ID <key>, toma results[0].urls.regular ?? urls.small, dispara best-effort GET a links.download_location con el mismo header, y devuelve {url, provider:'unsplash', attribution:{photographer, photographerUrl, source:'Unsplash', sourceUrl}}. (c) solo PEXELS_API_KEY -> unsplashKey falsy, se salta la rama 4a y entra la rama Pexels sin cambios (src.large||medium||original). (d) fallo de red/5xx/4xx de Unsplash -> try/catch o res.ok=false dentro de searchUnsplash devuelve {url:null}; el helper nunca lanza al flujo principal, asi que Deno.serve responde status 200. (e) cero resultados de Unsplash -> results.length===0 -> {url:null} 200. (f) el download trigger lanza/falla -> va en su propio try/catch (console.error) y la foto se devuelve igual. Se conservan intactos: validacion JWT (admin.auth.getUser), requisito de home_id, CORS/OPTIONS, POST-only, y no consumo de credito de IA. El try/catch de ultimo recurso de Deno.serve sigue degradando a {url:null}. Banner superior actualizado (Unsplash-first / Pexels-fallback / degradar, formato Client-ID, download trigger, UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY desde panel web de Supabase, deploy automatico por CI; se elimino la nota manual de `supabase functions deploy`). Credito visible del fotografo en UI queda documentado como mejora futura. Verificacion Dart (toolchain en /opt/flutter): dart format --set-exit-if-changed . -> 0 cambios; flutter analyze -> No issues found; flutter test -> 62 passed. Byproducts de flutter pub get (pubspec.lock, registrants linux/windows/macos, generated_plugins.cmake, analysis_options.yaml) restaurados con git restore; el commit contiene solo index.ts.
